audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gave Tryndamere levels 2, 3, first item and called level 6 Skill, in a 49.92% matchup where Poppy holds every tool that stops him.
audit.why: The already-audited mirror moved rows 1, 2, 4 and 5 to Poppy and left row 6 with Tryndamere. Steadfast Presence stops dashes outright — Spinning Slash is his only gap-close and only escape — and Heroic Charge stuns flat against any wall from 475.
audit.corrected: Skill, Poppy, Poppy, Skill, Poppy, Poppy, Tryndamere with ratings 5,4,4,5,4,4,6, in matched full/content pairs.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 was written as the moment Tryndamere takes over, and Keeper's Verdict was dismissed as something you 'eat and re-engage' through.
audit.why: Keeper's Verdict is a 140/120/100s channel that knocks enemies very far away. Against a 400-range melee with a 5-second immortality window, being thrown out of range does not need to kill you — it spends your entire ultimate for nothing. The real Tryndamere spike is two items.
audit.corrected: Level 6 given to Poppy with the reason stated; the flip moved to 2+ items.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page said Steadfast Presence 'knocks you down mid-cast' and never gave a cooldown for anything.
audit.why: Riot's text: activating Steadfast Presence stops enemy dashes around her, and a stopped dash leaves the enemy slowed and grounded — grounded, not knocked down, which matters because it means you cannot then dash out either. It also passively scales her Armor and Magic Resist up as her health drops, so the longer the trade the worse it gets. Hammer Shock is 8/7/6/5/4s, Heroic Charge 14/13/12/11/10s at 475 range, Steadfast Presence 20/18/16/14/12s.
audit.corrected: Grounding stated in spikes[1] and mid; the four cooldowns written into the phases and whys.

audit.whatIsWrong: Poppy is female; several breakdown and report fields called her 'he' and 'his'.
audit.why: The tldr and whys already use 'her', so the page contradicts itself within one screen.

edits.after: Levels 4-5 even out — Heroic Charge runs 14-10s and you can bait it.

edits.after: Level 6 is hers — Keeper's Verdict throws you out of it.

edits.before: Your R Undying Rage beats her — bait her E Heroic Charge and W into your ult window, survive, and Q Bloodlust the crit heal to turn. Just be careful of her R Keeper's Verdict knocking you away to deny a kill; it doesn't burst you, so eat it and re-engage.
edits.after: Undying Rage stops the kill, but Keeper's Verdict on 140/120/100s throws you far out of range and spends the whole window for nothing — bait it, or ult only once it has landed. Steadfast Presence stops Spinning Slash outright, leaving you slowed and grounded.

edits.before: Level 2 is a skill test, level 3 is yours, but level 4 tilts to Poppy: her W Steadfast Presence cancels your E Spinning Slash dash and her E Heroic Charge stun into a wall is a real punish, so hold E and fight only when her stun is down.
edits.after: Level 2 is already hers: Hammer Shock zones on an 8s cooldown and Heroic Charge stuns you into any wall from 475. Steadfast Presence stops Spinning Slash outright and leaves you slowed and grounded, so hold E and fight only once her stun is spent.

edits.before: From 6 and your first crit item onward you dominate — R Undying Rage survives her combo, her R Keeper's Verdict only displaces you rather than killing you, and your crits out-DPS a peel tank you out-duel whenever your ult is up.
edits.after: From two items you take over — Undying Rage survives her combo, Keeper's Verdict displaces you rather than killing you, and your crits out-DPS a peel tank you out-duel whenever your ult is banked and no wall sits behind you.

notes: The mirror's note that this page called Tryndamere 'sustain-less' while telling the player to build anti-heal appears to have been fixed on the Poppy side; the Tryndamere-side strings in this brief no longer contain that phrase. Worth flagging for the user: Steadfast Presence grounding a stopped dash means Spinning Slash is both your entry and your exit, and losing it to her W is what turns a trade into a death — that is now stated in mid and spikes[1] but it may deserve a dosFull slot of its own on a later pass.
